newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour cements second place in TV3 poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour cements second place in TV3 poll.

text.p: The first New Zealand opinion poll taken since a TV leaders' debate last Thursday shows the opposition Labour Party cementing its second place and its leader Helen Clark doubling her rating as preferred prime minister.
The TV3/CM Research Gallup poll of 500 voters, released on Monday, showed the ruling National Party's support down one to 37 percent among decided voters.
Labour was up two to 21 percent.
The government's potential coalition partners had mixed fortunes, with the morals-based Christian Coalition down to 3.4 percent from 5.8 in the previous TV3 poll taken two weeks ago.
Free-market ACT New Zealand jumped from 4.6 percent to 6.1 percent, the first time it has broken through the five percent threshold in a TV3 poll.
Parties which do not win one of the 65 electorate seats must get at least five percent in the party vote to qualify for seats in the single chamber parliament.
Labour's potential coalition partners firmed slightly with the left wing Alliance up one at 14 percent and economic nationalist New Zealand First also up one at 16 percent.
Of the 500 voters polled 16 percent were undecided.
Labour fared much better in the poll of voters' preferences in the 65 electorate seats with 28 percent support, up three. National was steady on 37 percent.
New Zealand First was up two to 16 percent and the Alliance down one to 11 percent.

Clark, the acknowledged victor of the leaders' debate, saw her rating as preferred Prime Minister jump from seven percent to 13 percent, more popular for the first time than Alliance leader Jim Anderton who scored 11 percent.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger was steady on 21 percent support with New Zealand First leader Winston Peters down one at 18 percent.
